name_en: Kufa juushii — firm-cooked pork-stock rice for festivals and rites
summary_ja: 豚だしで米を炊きこむ、しっかりとした歯ごたえの沖縄の炊き込みご飯。行事や祝いの日に欠かせないハレの料理で、盆の精霊迎えには葉ショウガ、冬至には田芋を加えるなど、季節ごとに姿を変える。
summary_en: Rice cooked firm in pork stock, its bite pronounced — one of two forms of Okinawan juushii, the other soft and porridge-like. Reserved for festivals and celebrations, it changes with the season: ginger leaf at Obon's spirit-welcoming, taro at the winter solstice.
source_title: クファジューシー 沖縄県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Yafara juushii — a soft, brothy rice porridge for an off day
summary_ja: だしをたっぷり効かせ、水分を多めにして炊く沖縄の雑炊風ご飯。しっかり炊き上げるクファジューシーに対し、日常の体調がすぐれない時にも食べやすいやわらかな仕立てで、よもぎや芋の葉を加える家庭も多い。
summary_en: A softer, wetter cousin of kufa juushii, cooked porridge-style with plenty of broth. Where the firmer version is festival food, this one is gentle enough to eat on an off day, and many households stir in mugwort or sweet-potato leaf.
source_title: ヤファラジューシー 沖縄県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Iiyachi — leaf-wrapped millet mochi carried through a harvest festival
summary_ja: もち米に粟や小豆を混ぜて大鍋で炊き、練り上げて芭蕉の葉で包んで蒸す竹富島の保存食。豊作を祈る種子取祭の間、祭事に追われて調理する時間がないため、すぐ食べられる携行食として用意されてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Mochi rice mixed with millet and red beans, cooked in a large pot, worked smooth, then wrapped in banana leaf and steamed — a keeping food from Taketomi Island. Made to eat on the go during the harvest-prayer Tanadui festival, when there's no time to cook amid the rites.
source_title: イーヤチ 沖縄県｜うちの郷土料理
